key_insight: A high-order multiscale method captures heterogeneous, fractionally damped wave propagation with a proven O(ε) global energy-norm error bound.
engineering_relevance: The method reduces the cost of simulating waves in composite materials with fine-scale heterogeneity and history-dependent attenuation.
method: Derive a homogenized wave equation with first- and second-order multiscale corrections.
Combine finite elements with an L2-1σ–Newmark time-discretization scheme.
Establish local residual cancellation, global error bounds, and unconditional shifted-energy stability.
evidence_signal: Two- and three-dimensional numerical examples demonstrate accuracy, efficiency, reduced computational cost, and robustness; the abstract reports no numerical speedup factors.
watch_item: Fractional damping requires temporal history treatment, so memory and runtime costs should be assessed for long-duration simulations.
paper_title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
